questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes sickle cell trait from sickle cell disease?
choices: Trait is always a mild pain-crisis disorder
Trait and disease require identical treatment
Trait usually represents carrier status and is not a milder form of recurrent sickle cell disease
Trait inevitably progresses to sickle cell disease
questions.explanation: Sickle cell trait is generally carrier status, not a mild form of SCD. The documented genotype and clinical history should guide interpretation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient with SCD reports severe pain typical of prior vaso-occlusive episodes. What is the safest nursing response?
choices: Delay analgesia until a laboratory test confirms the crisis
Use the individualized pain plan, give prescribed analgesia promptly, and reassess pain, function, sedation, and respirations
Label repeated requests as drug-seeking behavior
Give unlimited IV fluid before assessing heart, kidney, and lung status
questions.explanation: No laboratory value confirms or excludes VOE pain. Timely individualized analgesia and frequent safety reassessment are essential, while new emergency features are evaluated concurrently.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which new finding cluster most strongly suggests acute chest syndrome?
choices: Stable chronic anemia without respiratory symptoms
Leg pain that improves with the usual plan
Chest pain, cough, fever, falling oxygen saturation, and increased work of breathing
A healed ulcer with unchanged skin color
questions.explanation: ACS can resemble pneumonia and may progress rapidly. New chest symptoms, fever, hypoxemia, tachypnea, or increased work of breathing require emergency evaluation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which patient with SCD should the RN assess first?
choices: A patient requesting a warm pack for typical stable leg pain
A patient with new facial droop and difficulty speaking
A patient asking about a future clinic appointment
A patient whose chronic hemoglobin is unchanged from baseline
questions.explanation: New focal neurologic deficits may indicate stroke. Activate the stroke pathway, identify last known baseline, and coordinate urgent SCD-specific evaluation and treatment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which fluid plan is safest during a vaso-occlusive episode?
choices: Give rapid unlimited fluid to every patient
Avoid all oral and IV fluid regardless of hydration
Assess hydration, losses, urine output, lungs, and cardiac and kidney reserve, then follow the individualized ordered goal
Use edema alone to calculate a fixed rate
questions.explanation: Dehydration should be corrected, but excess fluid can worsen pulmonary complications. Fluid type and rate require individualized assessment and reassessment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient with SCD reports a painful erection that has lasted four hours. What should the RN do?
choices: Protect privacy and arrange emergency hematology and urology evaluation
Tell the patient to wait until the next routine visit
Apply stigma-based counseling before assessing onset
Document it as an expected harmless finding
questions.explanation: Priapism lasting four hours or more is an emergency because permanent tissue injury can occur. Rapid, private, nonjudgmental escalation is required.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Why should the RN compare the current hemoglobin with the patient's usual baseline?
choices: Every person with SCD has the same normal hemoglobin
A chronic low value may be usual, while a rapid symptomatic fall can indicate an acute complication
Baseline comparison eliminates the need to assess symptoms
A single value identifies the cause of anemia
questions.explanation: Baseline varies among patients. The magnitude and speed of change, symptoms, reticulocyte response, and clinical context help identify acute severe anemia.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A hospitalized patient with SCD develops fever. Which interpretation is safest?
choices: Fever is expected during every pain episode
Functional loss of splenic protection can increase severe infection risk, so the SCD fever pathway should be followed promptly
Antibiotics should always wait until all test results return
A well appearance rules out serious infection
questions.explanation: Fever may signal rapidly progressive infection in SCD. Follow the patient-specific and local emergency pathway, including timely ordered cultures and antimicrobials.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding after a recent transfusion requires urgent evaluation for delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction?
choices: Improving energy with stable urine color
Worsening anemia, jaundice, dark urine, fever, or increased pain
A stable old bruise
Normal appetite without symptoms
questions.explanation: Delayed hemolysis can appear after transfusion with falling hemoglobin, jaundice, dark urine, fever, fatigue, or pain. The blood bank and hematology team need prompt notification.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding best shows safe improvement after treatment of a vaso-occlusive pain episode?
choices: Lower pain score with increasing somnolence and shallow breathing
Improved function and patient-defined pain goal with stable respirations, oxygenation, and alertness
No pain assessment because the patient is asleep
Unchanged severe pain with falling oxygen saturation
questions.explanation: Effective treatment improves pain and function without unsafe sedation or respiratory compromise. Respirations, alertness, oxygenation, and adverse effects must be reassessed.
